correctness.rationale: The local criterion is diameter at most two and exclusion of the full square containing both geodesic midpoints of any selected distance-two pair. Normalize such a pair to 0 and e_1+e_2. With one midpoint selected every allowed point is in the ball about that midpoint; with neither, the nonzero points are weight-two supports which meet pairwise. If there is a common coordinate they yield a ball, and otherwise the edges must be exactly a triangle, giving a parity tetrahedron. The case with no distance-two pair has size at most two and is in a ball. Leaves in a ball have an alternative midpoint outside it, and both midpoints of each tetrahedron pair have the opposite parity. A tetrahedron is not contained in a ball, and distinct balls intersect in at most two points. Hence both kinds are facets (including d=3), and ball subfaces of size at least three are counted once. The number of distinct parity tetrahedra is 2^(d−2) times binom(d,3); the coefficients for sizes 0, 1, 2 follow by the direct unordered pair count. The independent geodesic test exhausts Q_3 and Q_4 and tests Q_5 up to size four; coefficient vectors are (1,8,24,32,10), (1,16,80,160,96,16), and (1,32,240,640,560) through size four, respectively. Direct augmentation gives facet counts {4:10} for Q_3 and {4:16,5:16} for Q_4. Replay: branches/4eb7a126-98b5-4c1f-a9ba-f27964bcd795/independent_check.py and independent_check.log. This is finite corroboration; the proof establishes all dimensions.
